interpretation: For each symmetry type X in {U, O, Sp}, a characteristic-polynomial limit gives a gamma-product candidate for g_{lambda,X}. Keeping Gamma(1+B_X(lambda)) visible is not cosmetic: absorbing it would hide the arithmetic origins of the moment parameters and the integrality of g_k at positive integers, whereas the quotient g_lambda/Gamma(1+B(lambda)) is precisely the nonvanishing meromorphic function of order two whose poles the paper describes. This normalization therefore separates an analytic object from arithmetic structure; agreement at small k calibrates, but does not prove, the conjectural transfer to L-function moments.

It then states both that g_lambda/Gamma(1+B(lambda)) is nonvanishing meromorphic of order two with completely described pole locations and that g_k is integral for positive integer k.

speculation_status: The meromorphic-quotient and positive-integer integrality claims are reported source results. The identification of the normalization as an analytic/arithmetic interface is an interpretation of those results. The L-function moment transfer remains conjectural, and low-k agreement is only calibration.

For every odd prime p, the orthogonal summand and each of the two exhaustive unitary residue cases are rewritten as integers strictly greater than -1, hence as nonnegative contributions; their sums give nonnegative odd-prime valuations. This representation gains a prime-by-prime, scale-by-scale certificate and exposes residue geometry hidden by the gamma-product form, but it depends on the exact floor conventions and does not itself supply the omitted p=2 argument.

Equations (5.1)-(5.3) show the orthogonal layer and the two unitary cases are greater than -1 and integral, so each is nonnegative. The span explicitly assumes p>2 and only says divisibility by a large power of 2 is easy.
